failure_patterns.pattern: rule_ignored: Answer kept words the clue already supplies or extra qualifiers instead of the bare head. 'Sirius Satellite Radio' for 'this satellite radio company', 'third Dalai Lama' for 'this title', 'Egg White Denver Omelet' for 'the Denver type of this'. 'Warren Gamaliel Harding' should be the standard 'Warren G. Harding'.

rejected_edits.content: - Passage TITLES are strong evidence. When there is no verbatim archive answer (or the snippets only repeat the clue), find the entity or headword that recurs across several titles alongside the clue's distinctive details (actor, director, columnist, a headcount, a quoted tagline). Examples: pages titled 'Phone Booth (film)', 'Eight Is Enough', 'Polonium', 'Funny Girl (1968)', or dictionary pages titled 'fume'. Take that recurring entity rather than a word from the clue or from a one-off passage, and give it in the short form the titles use, without 'film', 'series' or 'element' labels.
rejected_edits.target: - Otherwise, build the answer from passages that match several of the clue's details.

rejected_edits.content: - 'In <film/show> <actor> played this <descriptor>' asks for the real person or character portrayed, not the actor or the film. Find the passage line that pairs the actor with the role ('Stuart Sutcliffe (Stephen Dorff)') and give the name form the passages repeat. 'This <relation> of <famous person> who wrote <book>' asks for the author, so answer with the person the title is tied to.
rejected_edits.target: - Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?

rejected_edits.content: - Check the DIRECTION and ROLE of the clue's verb when the passages name two parties for the same event ('took control of', 'took over', 'acquired' vs 'handed over', 'relinquished', 'sold'). Answer the party that fits the verb: 'On Dec. 31, 1999 this country took control of the canal' -> 'Panama', not the US that gave it up.
rejected_edits.target: Do not talk yourself out of a well-supported entity.
